title: Jigsaw Structure
description: Defines a jigsaw structure that generates in the world using template pools and structure sets. A Jigsaw Structure is a dynamic, modular structure composed of multiple Structure Templates connected via Jigsaw Blocks. Each Structure Template contains Jigsaw Blocks that define how it can connect to other templates and where those connections should occur; these blocks act as connectors, enabling the structure to grow by attaching new pieces. Construction begins by placing a single template; any Jigsaw Blocks within it are added to a pending list, and the system recursively expands the structure by resolving those connections until the specified max_depth is reached. Examples of Jigsaw Structures include Trail Ruins and Trial Chambers.
note: Currently only Trail Ruins can be modified via JSON with the Data-Driven Jigsaw Structure Experimental Toggle turned on. Other Jigsaw Structures such as Villages and Bastions use a legacy version of the Jigsaw Structure System and cannot be modified via JSON.
note2: This generation process can be relatively time consuming depending on the complexity and quantity of Jigsaw Blocks in any given template.
technicalDescription: The overall behavior and placement of a Jigsaw Structure in the world are governed by its Jigsaw Structure JSON, which defines generation rules and constraints. For more info, see the Introduction to Jigsaw Structures documentation.

fields.title: Format Version
fields.description: The format version of this jigsaw structure definition.

fields.title: Jigsaw Definition
fields.description: The jigsaw structure definition.

fields.title: Description
fields.description: The description block containing the structure identifier. Must include a namespace; the 'minecraft' namespace must not be used unless overriding a vanilla structure.

fields.title: Biome Filters
fields.description: Array of filter conditions that determine which biomes can generate this structure. Biome filters are a type of Entity Filter that iterate only over biomes; most useful is the 'has_biome_tag' test paired with a value naming the biome tag to match.
fields.note: Jigsaw structures may behave unpredictably in dimensions other than the Overworld. Target Jigsaw Structures to overworld-specific biomes to prevent them from appearing unintentionally in other dimensions.

fields.title: Generation Step
fields.description: The world generation step during which this structure generates. This is used as a grouping concept to keep similar world-generation features bundled together and to order structures against each other.

choices.description: Step 1.

fields.title: Terrain Adaptation
fields.description: How the terrain should adapt relative to the generated Jigsaw Structure. 'Beard' refers to mass added below structures that would otherwise float in air.

choices.title: None
choices.description: Do not adjust ambient block density.

choices.title: Bury
choices.description: Ambient block density is added to all pieces of the structure, but only within the Y bounds of its starting piece. Ideal for structures that need to bury below the surface while letting another set of pieces stick up through the terrain uncovered.

choices.title: Beard (Thin)
choices.description: Ambient block density is added below the structure and block density is reduced just above the ground.

choices.title: Beard (Box)
choices.description: Ambient block density is added below the structure, and block density is reduced within the entire box the structure occupies.

choices.title: Encapsulate
choices.description: Ambient block density is added all around every piece of the structure.

fields.title: Start Pool
fields.description: Identifier of the Template Pool to use as the starting point for structure generation. A Structure Template is randomly chosen from this pool and placed as the first piece.

fields.title: Start Jigsaw Name
fields.description: The name of the Jigsaw Block from the start_pool to be placed first. Optional.

fields.title: Maximum Depth
fields.description: Maximum recursion depth for jigsaw piece connections. For example, a road structure with max_depth of 5 will have paths at most 5 templates long in any direction from the origin.

fields.title: Start Height
fields.description: Height provider that gives the offset at which the structure's start_pool should begin generating. This is an offset from the heightmap_projection; when heightmap_projection is set, the 'absolute' Vertical Anchor is recommended for ease of use.

fields.title: Type
fields.description: Height provider type. Determines the rest of the parameters in this object.

choices.title: Constant
choices.description: Single constant anchor point. Use 'value' to specify the Vertical Anchor.

choices.title: Uniform
choices.description: Uniform distribution of possible anchor points. Use 'min' and 'max' (each a Vertical Anchor) to bound the range.

fields.title: Value
fields.description: The Vertical Anchor to use as the constant height. Used only when type is 'constant'.

fields.title: Min
fields.description: The Vertical Anchor to use as the minimum of the uniform distribution. Used only when type is 'uniform'.

fields.title: Max
fields.description: The Vertical Anchor to use as the maximum of the uniform distribution. Used only when type is 'uniform'.

fields.title: Heightmap Projection
fields.description: Heightmap to use when determining the starting height.

choices.title: None
choices.description: Do not perform any heightmap projection; begin generating from a Y of 0.

choices.title: World Surface
choices.description: Begin generating relative to the first non-air block encountered from the top down.

choices.title: Ocean Floor
choices.description: Begin generating relative to the first motion-blocking block encountered from the top down.

fields.title: Dimension Padding
fields.description: Padding at the top and bottom of the dimension when placing the structure. Prevents the structure from creating holes in the bedrock or being cut off at the top. May be a positive integer (applied to both bounds) or an object specifying 'top' and 'bottom' separately.

fields.title: Bottom
fields.description: Distance in blocks from the bottom of the dimension that may not be used by the Jigsaw Structure.

fields.title: Top
fields.description: Distance in blocks from the top of the dimension that may not be used by the Jigsaw Structure.

fields.title: Maximum Distance From Center
fields.description: Maximum horizontal and vertical distance from jigsaw pieces to the structure start.

fields.title: Horizontal
fields.description: Maximum horizontal distance in blocks. Must be between 1 and 128 inclusive.

fields.title: Vertical
fields.description: Maximum vertical distance in blocks. Must be greater than 1.

fields.title: Pool Aliases
fields.description: Rewires jigsaw pool connections by redirecting pool references within an individual structure. Allows thematic substitution across a full structure. For example, an alias 'chambers/melee' can be replaced by 'chambers/melee/normal', 'chambers/melee/poison', or 'chambers/melee/wither' which are specialized Template Pools.

fields.title: Type
fields.description: The type of pool alias, which determines what other fields are valid.

choices.title: Direct
choices.description: Replaces a single alias with a single target. Requires 'alias' and 'target'.

choices.title: Random
choices.description: Replaces an alias with one of a weighted random list of targets. Requires 'alias' and 'targets'.

choices.title: Random Group
choices.description: Selects one of several groups of aliases via a weighted random list. Requires 'groups'. Groups may contain 'direct' or 'random' aliases (not nested 'random_group').

fields.title: Alias
fields.description: Identifier of the Template Pool to replace. Used by 'direct' and 'random' aliases.

fields.title: Target
fields.description: Identifier of the Template Pool to substitute when matched. Used by 'direct' aliases.

fields.title: Targets
fields.description: A weighted random list of potential Template Pools to choose from when the alias matches. Each entry has a 'data' (the target pool identifier) and a positive 'weight'. Used by 'random' aliases.

fields.title: Groups
fields.description: A weighted random list of groups of aliases. Each entry has a 'data' (an array of nested 'direct' or 'random' alias items) and a positive 'weight'. Used by 'random_group' aliases.

fields.title: Liquid Settings
fields.description: How to handle waterloggable blocks that overlap with existing liquid in the world.

choices.title: Apply Waterlogging
choices.description: Waterloggable blocks become waterlogged where they overlap existing liquid.

choices.title: Ignore Waterlogging
choices.description: Do not waterlog any waterloggable blocks that overlap existing liquid.
